notes: Public primary literature is deliberately selected to contain materially conflicting evidence. The scenario tests whether PPL Research preserves scientific disagreement as inconclusive instead of averaging it into a qualified/ready result. Literature triangulation is not treated as strong validation.

payload.question: Does bilingual experience produce a replicable executive-function advantage over monolingualism?

payload.text: Bilingual experience produces a replicable executive-function advantage over monolingualism in at least some non-language tasks or populations.

payload.summary: Three Simon-task studies reported smaller Simon costs for bilingual middle-aged/older adults, with a larger advantage in older participants.

source.title: Bilingualism, aging, and cognitive control: evidence from the Simon task

payload.summary: A meta-analysis of 170 studies reported task- and age-dependent bilingual advantages, with larger effects in samples aged 50+.

source.title: Meta-Analysis Reveals a Bilingual Advantage That Is Dependent on Task and Age

payload.summary: Across three studies and 15 executive-processing indicators, the critical bilingual Group×Condition interaction was significant for only one indicator and in the disadvantage direction.

source.title: There is no coherent evidence for a bilingual advantage in executive processing

payload.summary: A meta-analysis of 152 adult studies found that small pre-correction advantages disappeared after publication-bias correction and concluded there was no systematic support for a general adult executive-function advantage.

source.title: Is bilingualism associated with enhanced executive functioning in adults? A meta-analytic review

payload.summary: In a demographically representative sample of 4,524 US children aged 9–10, the ABCD study found little evidence of bilingual advantages in inhibitory control, attention, task switching, or cognitive flexibility.

source.title: No evidence for a bilingual executive function advantage in the nationally representative ABCD study
